runtime_expectations.reason: This is the first group in which the FastAPI application exists and is runnable: E1-S4 creates backend/src/app/main.py (the app factory) and backend/src/app/routers/health.py (GET /health), started per project-manifest.json's verification.local.start_commands as `cd backend && uv run uvicorn src.app.main:app --reload` (confirmed against the checked-out project-manifest.json — the `src.app.main:app` form, not `app.main:app`, matching the import-path deviation recorded in Group A note 3a and carried forward unchanged through Group B). The evaluator MUST run the health-check retry/backoff loop (5 retries, 2s backoff per project-manifest.json's verification.health_check) against http://localhost:8000/health before running api_checks and performance_checks. No other route is registered on main.py by this group — E2-S1 (auth) is a Service-layer story with no router yet (POST /api/auth/login is E2-S2, group D), and E3-S1/E4-S1/E5-S1/E6-S1/E7-S1/E8-S1/E9-S1 are Repository-layer stories with no router. A request to any path other than GET /health or the FastAPI-generated /docs and /openapi.json is expected to 404 in this group and is not a contract failure. The frontend toolchain still does not exist (group E creates it), so frontend_url is not probed. All repository-level and service-level assertions (unit_test_checks below) run offline against pytest/mypy/ripgrep/detect-secrets and do not require the running app; only the api_checks section requires the live server.

api_checks.description: E1-S4 AC1, AC4, AC5; api-contracts.md §4.1. No Authorization header sent — the endpoint is public. Response JSON contains status: 'ok' and database: 'connected' (a version field may also be present per api-contracts.md's example body and api-contracts.schema.json's HealthResponse, which lists version as optional with additionalProperties: false — its exact value is not asserted here since it is not fixed by any AC, but if present it must be a string). Must return 200 even though the only rows in the database beyond migrations are seed data — no test-only reset is performed before this probe.

E1-S4 AC2. A caller-supplied X-Request-ID is echoed back on the response (or, if the middleware always generates its own id per request, the response carries a stable X-Request-ID header of some value) so the evaluator can assert the header is present at all — the middleware's job is correlating log lines within one request, not necessarily honoring a caller-supplied id verbatim; either behavior satisfies AC2 as long as a request-id header is present on the response and the same value appears in the structured log line(s) emitted for this request (cross-checked against captured stdout/log output, not just the HTTP response, per unit_test_checks ut-047).

performance_checks.description: NFR-07 / E1-S4 AC1: GET /health responds within 1 second of the application completing startup. The evaluator's probe (after the health_check retry/backoff window in project-manifest.json succeeds at least once) times a fresh request and asserts it completes in under 1000ms. The 503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE branch (api-contracts.md §4.1 errors table) is NOT exercised by this live probe. Two live-fault-injection alternatives were considered and rejected at evaluator sign-off: (a) breaking the DB connection on the evaluator's own running instance mid-evaluation would corrupt the shared app under test for every other check in this group, and there is no way to restore it cleanly before the next check without a full app restart; (b) renaming/removing the underlying SQLite file out from under a live engine to simulate an outage is unreliable on Windows specifically (the platform this harness runs on — see env info), where an open file handle held by a pooled connection typically blocks the rename/delete outright rather than producing the clean 'connection refused'-style failure a POSIX host would give, making the result non-deterministic. A third alternative — starting a second, isolated uvicorn process on a different port with a deliberately invalid DATABASE_URL, probing its /health, then tearing it down — would exercise the real endpoint code path live without touching the primary instance, but was rejected as disproportionate to the payoff: it adds a second process-lifecycle (port allocation, startup race, cleanup-on-failure) to the evaluator's own responsibilities for one already-well-covered branch. That branch is instead covered by backend/tests/api/test_health.py with a monkeypatched connectivity probe (ut-046) — see architecture_checks.layering for exactly which module (backend/src/db/session.py or backend/src/db/engine.py) the probe is implemented against, which is also the monkeypatch target.

layering.command: rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?app\b" backend/src/domain backend/src/db ; rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?domain\.[a-z_]+\.(repository|threshold_repository)\b" backend/src/app ; rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?db\.models\b" backend/src/app ; rg -n "raise HTTPException" backend/src/domain
layering.description: Four static scans, each must return no matches (exit 1). (1) Neither backend/src/domain nor backend/src/db imports app/ anywhere — no domain or repository module may reach upward into the API layer. (2) backend/src/app (this group: main.py, routers/health.py, error_handlers.py, middleware/) imports no domain repository module directly — neither `domain.<name>.repository` nor `domain.<name>.threshold_repository`, matching the actual import convention already established in this codebase (`from src.domain.auth.repository import (...)`, confirmed by reading backend/tests/repository/test_user_repository.py). (3) backend/src/app also does not import backend/src/db/models.py directly — this is a NEW scan added at evaluator sign-off (see the layering-resolution note below); it closes the gap where a router could otherwise import an ORM table class and hand-roll a business query, bypassing the repository/service layers even while nominally staying within 'db/'. (4) No 'raise HTTPException' appears anywhere under backend/src/domain — service-layer code (this group: domain/auth/service.py) raises typed domain exceptions from backend/src/types/errors.py only; HTTP-status mapping is error_handlers.py's job exclusively. The optional `src.` prefix in patterns (1)-(3) is carried forward from Group A/B for the same reason recorded there — the delivered pyproject.toml resolves modules as `src.<layer>.*`, not as bare top-level packages.
layering.resolution_note: LAYERING RESOLUTION — the most consequential judgment call in this group's contract, made at evaluator sign-off after re-reading both directory-to-layer tables side by side. folder-structure.md §4's table gives API's 'May import from' as 'types, core, services' with no explicit 'May NOT' column, and a plain-language callout beneath it: 'a router may not import a repository.' Read in isolation, and with `backend/src/db/` grouped under that same table's 'Repository' row, this could be misread as forbidding GET /health's own connectivity probe from touching db/ at all. system-design.md §2.1's table is the more precise source and is the one this evaluator follows: its API row states 'May import from: types, core, domain/*/service.py' and 'May NOT import from: domain/*/repository.py (routers never reach past the service layer)' — the prohibition is textually scoped to `domain/*/repository.py`, not to `backend/src/db/` as a whole, which folder-structure.md's own tree diagram separately labels '# REPOSITORY LAYER (shared infrastructure)' — a distinct thing from a BRD-bounded-domain repository. This reading is independently corroborated by already-delivered, evaluator-approved code from group B: `backend/src/db/session.py`'s docstring states outright that 'request-scoped injection (`get_session` in `app/dependencies.py`) is added by E2-S2 and builds directly on `get_session_factory()`' — i.e. group B's own design already commits `app/` to importing `db/session.py` directly, one group later, and this contract would be inconsistent with that already-committed precedent if it forbade the same pattern here. RESOLUTION: GET /health's connectivity probe (this group) — and, by the same precedent, `app/dependencies.py`'s `get_session` (E2-S2, group D) — may import `backend/src/db/session.py` and/or `backend/src/db/engine.py` directly (e.g. opening a connection and executing a trivial `SELECT 1`), but may NEVER import `backend/src/db/models.py` (no ORM table class reaches app/) and may NEVER import any `domain/*/repository.py` or `*_repository.py` module. This is narrower than the generator's original draft, which permitted 'db/session.py and db/engine.py ... this import is permitted' without excluding db/models.py explicitly — scan (3) above closes exactly that gap. FLAGGED TO THE LEAD: folder-structure.md §4's table is imprecise relative to system-design.md §2.1's and should be amended to state the db/-vs-domain/*/repository.py distinction explicitly, the same way system-design.md already does, so this does not need re-litigating in a later group.

no_float.description: backend/tests/architecture/test_no_float_in_domain.py's SCANNED_PACKAGES already globs backend/src/db and backend/src/domain recursively (confirmed by reading the delivered module: `SCANNED_PACKAGES = ("src/types", "src/core", "src/db", "src/domain")`), so no change to SCANNED_PACKAGES itself is required for this group's 7 new domain subpackages (audit, risk_profile, recommendation, holdings, goals, rebalancing, advisor) or for models.py's growth — they are picked up automatically by the existing rglob. What component-map.md note 5 requires this group to ADD is a new assertion extending `test_the_scan_covers_group_a_and_group_b_source_trees` (or an equivalent parametrized case) that explicitly enumerates these 7 new subpackage directory names as present under the scan, so a future accidental narrowing of SCANNED_PACKAGES is caught by a named test rather than silently passing because the glob happened to still include them — mirroring the existing test's own pattern of asserting `{"types", "core", "db", "domain", "auth"} <= scanned`. Every money column (target_amount, current_value, nav_value, threshold_bps — E6-S1 AC5, E7-S1 AC4) and every percent/bp column added to models.py this group is SQLAlchemy Integer/Mapped[int]; no float literal, float() call or -> float annotation appears anywhere in the 7 new repository modules, threshold_repository.py, domain/auth/service.py, core/security.py, core/logging.py, or the app/ package. The module's existing non-vacuity self-check (`test_the_detector_recognises_a_float_annotation`) must still pass unmodified.

append_only.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/architecture/test_append_only.py
append_only.description: backend/tests/architecture/test_append_only.py is CREATED by this group's E3-S1 (component-map.md's E3-S1 row lists it explicitly) and gains one case for E9-S1's AdvisorOverride repository (component-map.md's E9-S1 row also lists it explicitly). Scope confirmed by re-reading component-map.md's test-file column for all 7 remaining repository-layer stories in this group, not merely assumed: E4-S1 (test_risk_profile_repository.py only), E5-S1 (test_allocation_template_repository.py + test_allocation_sum.py), E6-S1 (test_holdings_repository.py + test_csv_loader.py), E7-S1 (test_goals_repository.py only) and E8-S1 (test_rebalancing_repository.py + test_threshold_repository.py) each list their own repository test file(s) and never test_append_only.py. This is also consistent with data-models.md's per-entity mutability markers, cross-checked directly (§4): RiskBandRule and AllocationTemplate are 'insert-only, immutable once published' (a versioned-publish pattern, not a bare no-update table); Goal is explicitly 'mutable (AC-03)' — 'one of only two genuinely mutable domain tables' — and E7-S1 AC5/ut-077 correctly requires an update_goal path rather than treating Goal as append-only; AssetClass is 'master data, mutable' and Holding is 'mutable (revalued each advance-a-day)', neither of which E6-S1's own ACs assert append-only behavior for (E6-S1 AC3 only claims NavSnapshot is append-only, which is correct per data-models.md §4.10); RebalancingRecommendation is 'append-only with one-shot status transition' — a controlled single in-place update of resolved_at, not a bare no-update table, matching ut-079/ut-081's design exactly. This architecture_check therefore asserts the shared module covers exactly what component-map.md attributes to it — AuditLogEntry and AdvisorOverride — typically via introspection (e.g. `inspect.getmembers` on the repository module asserting no callable name starts with `update_` or `delete_` for these two tables) rather than reflection over the whole domain/ tree, so it does not silently mask the other stories' checks living in their own files.

folder_structure.description: Every path in files_must_exist sits exactly where folder-structure.md §2 and component-map.md place it: the API layer additions under backend/src/app/ (routers/, middleware/, error_handlers.py) and backend/src/core/logging.py; domain/auth/service.py and core/security.py for E2-S1; and one new package per remaining repository story under backend/src/domain/ (audit/, risk_profile/, recommendation/, holdings/, goals/, rebalancing/ [containing both repository.py and threshold_repository.py, per component-map.md's E8-S1 row], advisor/), each containing exactly the file(s) its component-map.md row names — no story creates a service.py, engine.py or pure-computation module (scoring.py, horizon.py, drift.py, progress.py, engine.py) this group; those are Group D/E stories, and no new domain package beyond the 9 named above is created (in particular, no domain/health/ package — see architecture_checks.layering's resolution note for why the health probe does not need one). MODELS-GROWTH ALLOWANCE (component-map.md note 2): backend/src/db/models.py is modified by 7 of this group's 9 stories (all but E1-S4 and E2-S1) and will very likely cross the check-file-length hook's 300-line hard limit once User/Customer's existing 52 lines gain ~13 more ORM classes (AuditLogEntry; RiskBandRule, RiskProfileAnswer, RiskBandAssignment; AllocationTemplate; AssetClass, NavSnapshot, Holding; Goal, GoalProgressSnapshot; RebalancingRecommendation, RebalancingThreshold; AdvisorOverride) at roughly 15-25 lines per class including constraints and docstring. If models.py reaches the 200-line warn threshold this group MAY split it into backend/src/db/models/ (one module per domain, e.g. models/audit.py, models/risk_profile.py, ..., re-exported through models/__init__.py) WITHOUT changing the import surface (`from src.db.models import AuditLogEntry` etc. must keep working) and WITHOUT thinning any constraint (component-map.md note 2 explicit: 'not thinned by removing constraints'). This check accepts either backend/src/db/models.py (single file, if it stays under 300 lines) OR backend/src/db/models/__init__.py plus per-domain submodules as satisfying every 'models.py' entry in files_must_exist — the evaluator resolves the path accordingly rather than treating a split as a missing-file failure.

unit_test_checks.assertion: A TestClient GET /health with no Authorization header returns 200 with a JSON body, both immediately after app startup and again after inserting zero additional rows beyond seed data — no auth dependency is registered on this route.

Response body's status field equals 'ok' and database field equals 'connected' when the DB connection succeeds. With backend/src/db/session.py's session-scope helper (or the backend/src/db/engine.py-level connection it wraps) monkeypatched to raise on use — the exact module the health probe is implemented against per architecture_checks.layering's resolution note — GET /health returns 503 with code DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE and body {'status':'degraded','database':'unavailable'}.

GET /health's response carries an X-Request-ID header, and every structured log line captured (via caplog or a stdout-capturing fixture) for that single request contains the same request-id value as a JSON field — proving the id is stable across the request's log entries, not merely present on the HTTP response.

Given a captured log record whose underlying request/response contained a password, password_hash, or a raw financial-position value (e.g. current_value, target_amount) in its body, the emitted structured JSON log line does not contain that field's raw value anywhere — either the field is absent from the log payload entirely or its value is replaced by a fixed redaction marker (e.g. '[REDACTED]'). Covers both an inbound request body and an outbound response body.

Given a correct email/password pair for a seeded user, the service returns a signed JWT whose decoded payload's sub equals the user's id (as a string) and role is one of customer|advisor|admin|compliance matching that user's stored role.

An incorrect password for an existing email, and a well-formed email that does not exist at all, both raise the identical generic invalid-credentials exception type/message — the two failure paths are indistinguishable to the caller, so no code path lets a caller infer whether the email exists.

core/security.py's verify function compares a plaintext candidate against a bcrypt hash via bcrypt's own checkpw/verify primitive (never string equality); with caplog attached, authenticating (success and failure cases) emits no log line containing the plaintext password anywhere.

A JWT issued with the clock frozen at T, then decoded with the clock advanced past T + jwt_access_token_expiry_minutes (E1-S2's config value), is rejected as invalid/expired; decoding the same token at T + (expiry - 1 minute) still succeeds.

domain/auth/service.py exposes no register/create-account-with-arbitrary-password function reachable from this service's public API; authenticate() called with an email not present among seeded users fails with the same generic invalid-credentials error as ut-050, never creating a row.

domain/audit/repository.py exposes insert_audit_entry and read/query functions only; inspecting the module's public callables finds none named update_* or delete_* for AuditLogEntry, and attempting to call any such name (getattr with a default) confirms it does not exist.
insert_audit_entry(...) persists a row whose columns round-trip exactly: entity_type, entity_id, actor_id, actor_role, action, timestamp, details_json, matching the values passed in.

Querying by entity_type and a date range, after inserting 3+ rows with distinct timestamps in non-chronological insertion order, returns them ordered by timestamp ascending; rows outside the entity_type or date range are excluded.

details_json accepted by insert_audit_entry contains only ids, enum values and version numbers in the test fixtures used across this suite (e.g. {'customer_id': 3, 'risk_band': 'MODERATE', 'rule_version': 1}); a documented/tested example demonstrates no raw PII (email, name) or raw financial value (a money/percent field) is ever passed as a details_json value in any call site exercised by this group's tests.

Inserting a RiskBandRule row round-trips version, questionnaire_json (containing >=6 question entries), scoring_rules_json, published_at, is_active; the repository module exposes no update_rule/update_risk_band_rule function.
After seeding one RiskBandRule and publishing a second version, get_active_rule() returns exactly one row (the newest), never zero and never both.
The module exposes no update_*/delete_* function for RiskProfileAnswer (getattr-with-default check); inserting two submissions for the same customer_id leaves both sets of rows queryable.

Seeding an initial rule produces version == 1 with is_active == true; publishing a second version produces version == 2 with is_active == true, and re-reading version 1 by its version number returns it with is_active now false, still fully queryable (questionnaire_json/scoring_rules_json unchanged).
Each inserted RiskProfileAnswer row round-trips customer_id, question_id, answer_value, submitted_at exactly as passed.

Inserting an AllocationTemplate whose allocations_json percent_bps values sum to 9900 or 10100 (not exactly 10000) raises at the repository boundary and persists no row; a sum of exactly 10000 succeeds.
The module exposes no update_* function for AllocationTemplate; a correction is only possible by inserting a new version row.

get_active_template('MODERATE') returns exactly one row after two versions are published for that band, and a distinct call for 'CONSERVATIVE' returns that band's own active row, never cross-contaminating bands.

After publishing version 2 for a band, version 1's row is still fetchable by (risk_band, version=1) with its original allocations_json intact and is_active now false; version numbers for the same band are strictly increasing and distinct.
Running the seed step produces exactly 6 AllocationTemplate rows: 2 versions for each of CONSERVATIVE, MODERATE, AGGRESSIVE, with the newer version is_active == true and the older false per band.

Running the CSV loader against an empty, freshly migrated database inserts 5-6 AssetClass rows (matching backend/seed/asset_classes.csv) and exactly one NavSnapshot row per AssetClass for the CSV's initial price_date, with nav_value matching backend/seed/nav_initial.csv.

Running the loader a second time against an already-seeded database leaves the AssetClass row count unchanged (unique constraint on code enforced, no IntegrityError propagates uncaught) and creates no duplicate NavSnapshot row for the same (asset_class_id, price_date).

domain/holdings/repository.py exposes no update_* function for NavSnapshot (getattr-with-default check); a new price for the same asset class on a later price_date is a new inserted row, not a rewrite of the existing one.
With three NavSnapshot rows for the same asset_class_id on three distinct, non-chronologically-inserted price_dates, get_latest_nav(asset_class_id) returns the row with the maximum price_date.

NavSnapshot.nav_value round-trips through the repository as an integer minor-units value (e.g. 13245 for '132.45'); the underlying SQLAlchemy column type is Integer/Mapped[int], never Float/Numeric-as-float, confirmed by introspecting the mapped column's Python type.
Creating three Goal rows for the same customer_id succeeds, each round-tripping target_amount, target_date, priority, created_at independently.
The module exposes no update_*/delete_* function for GoalProgressSnapshot (getattr-with-default check); a recomputed snapshot for a new price_date is a new inserted row.
With three GoalProgressSnapshot rows for the same goal_id at three distinct snapshot_at timestamps inserted out of order, get_latest_progress(goal_id) returns the row with the maximum snapshot_at.
Goal.target_amount round-trips as an integer minor-units value through the repository; the mapped column's Python type is int, never float.

A documented update function (e.g. update_goal(...)) changes target_amount and/or priority on an existing Goal row in place without inserting a new row and without altering created_at, while updated_at moves forward — distinct from the separate append-only GoalProgressSnapshot insert path exercised by ut-074/ut-075. Consistent with data-models.md §4.7: Goal is explicitly documented as one of only two genuinely mutable domain tables.
Inserting a RebalancingRecommendation persists status == 'pending', the given proposed_actions_json, generated_at, and a resolved_at of None/null.

Transitioning a pending row to 'accepted' (and, in a second row, to 'dismissed') sets resolved_at to a non-null timestamp and leaves the row's id, customer_id and proposed_actions_json unchanged — no new row is created and the original row is never deleted.

The module exposes no hard-delete function for RebalancingRecommendation (getattr-with-default check) — neither delete_recommendation nor any DELETE-issuing callable is reachable from the module's public API.

Calling the accept/dismiss transition a second time on an already-resolved recommendation raises (does not silently succeed or silently no-op) and leaves status and resolved_at exactly as set by the first transition.
get_pending(customer_id) returns only rows with status == 'pending' for that customer, excluding both that customer's resolved rows and another customer's pending rows.

notes: 1. Shared-file sequencing (backend/src/db/models.py, backend/src/db/seed.py). Of this group's 9 stories, 7 modify models.py (all but E1-S4 and E2-S1) and 5 modify seed.py (E4-S1, E5-S1, E6-S1, E7-S1, E8-S1 — not E3-S1's AuditLogEntry, which the seed step never pre-populates, and not E9-S1's AdvisorOverride, which is created only through advisor action, never seeded). This contract does not prescribe the generator team's internal write-ordering for those two files — that is the generator's coordination problem to solve — but the checks below are written so they hold regardless of ordering: files_must_exist checks final-state presence only; the no_float, append_only and allocation_sum architecture checks scan the finished tree; and every unit_test_check targets one story's own table(s) in isolation, so a partial or interleaved integration of models.py does not cause a check attributed to a different story to fail as a side effect, as long as the final models.py contains all 13 new ORM classes with their documented constraints intact.

2. models.py may legitimately exceed a single file and split into backend/src/db/models/ (see architecture_checks.folder_structure's MODELS-GROWTH ALLOWANCE). This was anticipated, not discovered: component-map.md note 2 states the split option explicitly. The evaluator resolves any files_must_exist entry naming db/models.py against either layout.

3. test_append_only.py and test_allocation_sum.py are new shared architecture-test modules, each with a narrow, explicit ownership this group (test_append_only.py: created by E3-S1 for AuditLogEntry, extended by E9-S1 for AdvisorOverride; test_allocation_sum.py: created and owned solely by E5-S1).
